Mesh Inference
A Formal Model of Collective Inference Without a Center

Hongwei Xu Affiliation: SYM.BOT Email: hongwei@sym.bot
June 2026
Abstract

We present a formal model of mesh inference: how a population of independent agents, each holding private state and exchanging only admitted, typed observations, derives a conclusion none of them holds alone, with no central coordinator and no agent exposed. No agent shares weights, gradients, or hidden state, and the agents may span different teams, networks, and organizations. Motivated by the observation that asking a model is energy-minimizing inference, we model the mesh as a coupled free energy that each agent relaxes locally. We show that a single admission/emission policy governs three properties. First, mesh inference converges to a unique answer for any admission, symmetric or not, because the coupling is always an M-matrix. Second, it is identification-complete: it derives the centralized optimum exactly when the contributing views are carrier-connected. Third, it is observation-only: no node transmits its internals, and confidentiality is the dual of identification—the same rank condition that recovers collective knowledge bounds the recovery of private knowledge. Content-addressed lineage is the only global side-channel. In the linear–Gaussian regime every derived answer is determined, hence equal to the centralized optimum, at O⁡(diam2)O(\mathrm{diam}^{2}) latency, the measured price of removing the center. One such derivation is one turn of a center-free learning loop, which we formalize as architecture rather than prove. The open problem we state is when asking improves the collective rather than corrupting it: whether the non-linear closure derives an upgraded answer or a confident error. To our knowledge, this is the first formal characterization of when a center-free, observation-only mesh recovers the centralized optimum.

1 Introduction

A growing body of agent protocols and “internet of agents” infrastructure lets autonomous agents communicate. The harder question is whether a population can reason together: derive a conclusion that the members jointly determine but none holds alone. We study this on a substrate where each agent runs on its own device, owns its data, and never emits its weights, gradients, or hidden state. We call the operation mesh inference. It is not recall of a stored answer. It is the derivation of a conclusion that no member could reach alone, composed from the members’ partial views, computed with no central coordinator and no agent exposed. The agents may belong to different teams, networks, and organizations. The conclusion is real, since it lives in the union of the members’ views, but reaching it through purely local interaction is not automatic. This paper characterizes the conditions under which it succeeds.

Mechanically, this reasoning is energy relaxation. Asking a model is, formally, energy-minimizing inference: modern associative memories store patterns as the minima of an energy whose relaxation dynamics is exactly transformer attention [9]. We adopt the same view. A question clamps coordinates of an energy, the dynamics relaxes, and the freed coordinates at equilibrium are the answer. We write the primitive that drives one such relaxation ask⁡(⋅)\mathrm{ask}(\cdot). The relaxation is the inference, and its fixed point is the answer. The remaining question is which sovereign substrates support it across a whole population. The answer is a condition on one object: the policy by which agents admit and re-emit observations.

The full picture is a loop. An agent runs mesh inference and applies the result. It then learns from what the application teaches and feeds that back, so the next inference, and the next agent with a similar problem, draws on more. This paper proves one turn of that loop: the collective’s answer is real, determined, and computed without exposing any agent. It formalizes the loop that the turn sits inside. And it identifies the open problem: whether, as the loop generalizes a learned answer to a new problem, the derived answer can be trusted.

Standard distributed-intelligence designs place a center at exactly this point. Federated learning [1] keeps an aggregator. The dominant multi-agent paradigm is centralized training with decentralized execution [2]. Decentralized SGD removes the parameter server but still optimizes a single shared model [14]. Retrieval-augmented models keep a central index [13]. For an architecture whose value is per-node sovereignty [12], that center is the object to remove. Removing it at inference time, not just at execution time, is the bar.

That collective capability is the competitive layer of multi-agent systems is no longer speculative. In 2026 the largest vendors moved to own it. OpenAI’s Frontier binds an enterprise’s agents to a shared knowledge layer over its CRM, ticketing, and data warehouses [42]. Microsoft’s Agent Framework supplies graph-based orchestration that routes a shared thread among agents [43]. Teradata folds multimodal embeddings into a single governed vector store [44]. A further class markets the property head-on: inference-mesh and agentic-mesh orchestration platforms—kamiwaza’s Inference Mesh the on-the-nose example—place compute beside the data and advertise answers no single node could produce, yet by their own account route each request to the relevant nodes and pool the outputs at a synthesizer that merges and reconciles them [45]. Each of these systems works, and each keeps a center: the enterprise platforms because they live inside one organization’s trust boundary, where a coordinator holds the data and a single owner hosts the index; the mesh-orchestration platforms because the synthesizer that routes and pools node outputs is itself a center, and the point at which those outputs are aggregated in the clear, wherever the nodes physically sit. In principle such systems perform collective inference. What they do not do is perform it without a center. Mesh inference addresses the regime that this boundary excludes: an internet of agents [34], where inference runs across teams, organizations, and networks, among parties that will not pool data, expose models, or appoint a host. There a center is not available, and sovereignty becomes the enabling condition.

The question is no longer whether agents can be orchestrated, but whether a population that shares nothing beyond admitted, typed observations can still answer collectively. This is not decentralization for its own sake: in the regime we target the center is not a component one declines but a host no participant will accept, so a center-free derivation is not the slower path to the answer but the only collective inference the setting admits. And the property it must deliver—that the answer is the real collective one, and that no member is exposed in reaching it—is a guarantee, which a deployment can assert but only a formal model can establish: when it holds, how it fails, and the single policy that decides both. That is why this operation must be proved, not merely built—and proving it is this paper.

Contributions.

We show that a sovereign, observation-only mesh can infer what its population knows collectively: the answer the members jointly determine but none holds alone. We characterize exactly when that inference equals the centralized optimum. One such inference is one turn of a center-free learning loop, which we also formalize. The contributions, tagged [proven] / [framework] / [open]:

  1. 1.

    [proven] A formal model of mesh inference (§3), built from first principles: the inference step ask⁡(⋅)\mathrm{ask}(\cdot) is clamp-and-relax on a local free energy, which is energy-based equilibrium inference made distributed and sovereign, with the admission/emission policy promoted to the single characterized object.

  2. 2.

    [proven] One policy governs three properties (§4–7): one unconditional, and two that are a single rank-and-connectivity condition read with opposite signs. Mesh inference is convergent unconditionally: the coupling is always an M-matrix, so it terminates at a unique answer for any admission, symmetric or not. The other two are the dual pair. It is identification-complete: it derives the answer no member holds, the centralized optimum, iff the policy satisfies provenance-aware admission and non-selective source-novel forwarding, with carrier-graph connectivity the exact criterion. And it is observation-only by the same condition sign-flipped: no node transmits weights, gradients, or raw state, and a private state stays confidential exactly where the adversary’s probes fail to span it—the rank-and-connectivity that lets the collective recover its answer is what bounds what an adversary recovers. All three reduce to one admission/emission policy, with content-addressed lineage the single global side-channel, and the member’s safety falls out of the very condition that gives the collective its answer. §10 gives the honest cost, a compression–identification–rate frontier dialed by anchor budget.

  3. 3.

    [framework] The learning loop (§11): the proven turn is the inference half of a cycle (ask, apply, learn from the world, feed back) in which the collective closure grows by empirical feedback. We formalize the dynamics as architecture, not theorems, bounded by the principle that the mesh manufactures no information: it accumulates only what agents learn by acting.

  4. 4.

    [open] The central open problem (§12): when asking improves the collective rather than corrupting it. This is generalization correctness in the non-linear closure, where an upgraded answer to a similar problem can be true or a confident error.

The ingredients are classical and not ours. The relaxation that drives each step is energy-based equilibrium inference in the sense of deep equilibrium models and equilibrium propagation [20, 21, 9, 17]; that a population minimizing local free energy performs inference no single member can is the multi-agent free-energy principle [4, 22, 23, 24]; and the construction further rests on predictive coding [3], potential games [5], consensus, synchronization, and distributed estimation [6, 7, 8, 15], graph signal processing [16]. What is not classical is the object itself. Communication between sovereign agents is handled, by interoperability protocols [34] and by federated retrieval [29, 30, 31]. What has had no formal model is the inference: how a sovereign mesh reasons, deriving what the population jointly determines but no member holds, across organizations, with no center and no member exposed, and whether that reasoning is sound. Mesh Cognition [12] names the architecture. This paper supplies what it lacked, and what, to our knowledge, no prior work provides: a formal characterization of mesh inference with mathematical guarantees (convergence, identification-completeness, and confidentiality) that reduce all three to one characterized object, the admission/emission policy under which the mesh derives what the population knows collectively but no member holds, reliably and without exposing any member.

2 Related Work

Equilibrium-based inference.

The inference step ask⁡(⋅)\mathrm{ask}(\cdot) is, formally, energy-based equilibrium inference: clamp a subset of coordinates, relax to a fixed point, read the rest. This is the setting of deep equilibrium models [20], which define an output as the implicit fixed point of a single layer, and of equilibrium propagation [21], whose inference phase clamps inputs and settles an energy to its minimum, with the continuous Hopfield network [9] as prototype and dense associative memory [17] as its high-capacity generalization. These fix the energy and the solver on a single device. Our contribution is to distribute the same operation across sovereign nodes that never share state, and to characterize when the distributed relaxation still returns the centralized fixed point.

Collective free-energy minimization.

That a population of agents each minimizing a local free energy can perform inference no single agent can is not new. It is the multi-agent reading of the free-energy principle [4]. Because free energy is extensive, agents minimizing their local free energy jointly minimize the ensemble’s [22], and recent work exhibits collectives holding information that exceeds any member’s internal model [23]. We take this principle as given, not as a result. That literature has begun to supply formal guarantees, such as posterior consistency and no-regret for free-energy-minimizing agents [27] and formal treatments of strategic multi-agent inference [28]. But these are in the single-agent and game-theoretic settings, not the distributed, observation-only regime we treat. Our characterization is of a different object: the conditions on the admission/emission policy under which the local relaxation is convergent, identification-complete, and observation-only, proved in the linear–Gaussian regime with explicit wire-level constraints.

Collective intelligence by sharing belief.

A parallel line makes collective intelligence depend on agents accessing one another’s internal states. Its programmatic statement is the active-inference “ecosystems of intelligence” vision [24]: an ecology that attains shared intelligence by sharing beliefs through a common modeling language and transaction protocol. Two models instantiate the mechanism: [25] endows active-inference agents, in stages, with Theory of Mind and goal alignment and watches system-level performance emerge in simulation; [26] builds a network of Bayesian agents that infer teammates’ beliefs from observed communication and lifts a human team’s performance above what its members reach unaided. In all three, the collective gain is carried by internals crossing the node boundary—an agent modeling, or receiving, another’s beliefs. Our regime forbids exactly that. Mesh inference is observation-only (§6, Prop. 2): no node represents, requests, or emits another’s internals; confidentiality is the dual of identification; and the collective optimum is reached by admitting and re-emitting typed observations rather than by sharing belief. The Theory-of-Mind and belief-sharing apparatus these works treat as the enabling capability is, in the linear–Gaussian regime, not required for identification-completeness. They also differ in kind—[24] a vision, [25] a simulation, [26] a human-subject study—and none states the admission/emission conditions under which a distributed relaxation returns the centralized optimum, which is the object we characterize.

Federated retrieval.

The applied analogue is federated retrieval-augmented generation, which answers queries over knowledge fragmented across devices without sharing raw data [29, 30, 31]. FD-RAG [29] targets multi-source queries over fragmented corpora, which is our setting, yet, like the rest of this line, it retains a coordinator that aggregates retrieved context. Our ask⁡(⋅)\mathrm{ask}(\cdot) has no such center. The answer is the fixed point of a coordinator-free relaxation, and we prove the conditions under which it equals the centralized result.

Local-as-view query answering.

The identification side of ask⁡(⋅)\mathrm{ask}(\cdot) has a precise formal neighbor in database theory: local-as-view (LAV) data integration, in which each source is described as a view over a global schema and a query is answered by composing the views that cover it [36, 37]. Our §5 is exactly this picture under a Gaussian metric. Each agent holds a lossy view yi=Ci​s⋆y_{i}=C_{i}s^{\star}, collective identifiability is view coverage (⋃irow⁡(Ci)\bigcup_{i}\mathrm{row}(C_{i}) full rank), and the carrier graph is view reachability. This is the LAV pattern in a linear instantiation, view-based least-squares recovery, rather than classical relational LAV (conjunctive-query rewriting, certain answers under an open world). The structural correspondence is exact; the query algebra is not. Classical LAV rewrites and routes the query at a mediator that holds the global view catalog, which is a center, precisely what §1 removes. We replace that catalog with content-addressed lineage (Lemma 3), so a node can tell where a direction originates with no central registry. Its inference-side cousin, Gaussian belief propagation, is exact in O⁡(diam)O(\mathrm{diam}) on tree-like carriers and converges under walk-summability [38], a condition implied by the diagonal dominance, and indeed the M-matrix structure, that our convergence already establishes. On loopy carriers it converges iteratively rather than in a single pass, at a rate set by the walk-summability margin, faster than Jacobi diffusion but not O⁡(diam)O(\mathrm{diam}) in general. A lineage-routed message-passing realization of ask\mathrm{ask} thus inherits our admission/emission conditions unchanged, and we state it as the latency program in §12.

Distributed associative memory.

Closest in mechanism is distributed associative memory. [32] performs energy-based associative retrieval through fully decentralized message passing, and [33] reconstructs latent archetypes from partial, noisy, heterogeneous observations across clients, both our exact retrieval form. The latter, however, ships each client’s Hebbian operator to a central server for aggregation. We remove the server, and beyond the retrieval rule we characterize the admission policy that determines whether retrieval succeeds at all.

Agent interoperability protocols.

A parallel effort standardizes how autonomous agents discover and message one another (MCP, A2A, ACP, and the decentralized ANP [34]), with recent work taking a semantic rather than transport view of these exchanges [35]. These define the envelope, not the cognition: none specifies an inference operator or a notion of collective identifiability. Our protocol [10] is the semantic memory layer such transports would carry; the two are complementary, not competing.

A disambiguation.

We distinguish our setting from “decentralized AI inference” in its now-dominant sense: markets that distribute the compute for an otherwise centralized model across rented or verifiable hardware (Render, Akash, Gensyn, and related DePIN networks). That decentralizes execution; we decentralize cognition, leaving each node’s model, state, and data in place.

Foundations and contribution.

The construction rests on classical results we use directly: distributed estimation and consensus [15, 6], potential games [5], synchronization [7, 8], graph signal processing [16], and predictive coding [3]. Against all of the above, our contribution is neither the energy-based inference step nor the collective-inference principle, both of which predate us, but their synthesis under sovereignty together with its formal characterization. To our knowledge, this is the first statement of the admission/emission policy conditions under which center-free, observation-only mesh inference is convergent, identification-complete, and equal to the centralized optimum.

3 A formal model of mesh inference

We build the model from first principles, in four moves: the substrate, meaning what a mesh is and what sovereignty forbids; the policy, the single object every guarantee will turn on; the inference dynamics, meaning how the mesh reasons, namely energy relaxation, of which ask\mathrm{ask} is one step; and the soundness program, the three properties mesh inference must satisfy to be a foundation one can build on: that it converges, that it derives what the population jointly determines, and that it exposes no member.

Definition 1 (Mesh).

A mesh, the substrate of the Mesh Memory Protocol [10], is a graph G=(V,E)G=(V,E) with agents V={1,…,N}V=\{1,\dots,N\} and neighborhoods NiN_{i}. Agent ii holds private state hi∈ℝdh_{i}\in\mathbb{R}^{d} and sovereign parameters xix_{i}, and emits a public, lossy, typed observation oi=gxi​(hi)∈ℝpo_{i}=g_{x_{i}}(h_{i})\in\mathbb{R}^{p}, p<dp<d. Only oio_{i} is transmitted; hi,xih_{i},x_{i} never leave ii. Observations are typed over fields FF with orthogonal projectors {Pf}f∈F\{P_{f}\}_{f\in F}. Each agent carries a private target τi\tau_{i} (its own data), which anchors it and prevents trivial collapse.

Definition 2 (Admission/emission policy).

Agent ii admits a neighbor’s observation through a receiver-autonomous, per-field gate

Ai​(oj)=∑f∈Fαi,f​β​(si,f​(oj))​mjf​(Pf​oj−Pf​o^i),o^i=gxi​(hi),A_{i}(o_{j})=\sum_{f\in F}\alpha_{i,f}\,\beta\!\big(s_{i,f}(o_{j})\big)\,m_{j}^{f}\,\big(P_{f}o_{j}-P_{f}\hat{o}_{i}\big),\qquad\hat{o}_{i}=g_{x_{i}}(h_{i}),

with sovereign weights αi,f≥0\alpha_{i,f}\geq 0, band-pass gate β∈[0,1]\beta\in[0,1] (admit the mid-band: neither redundant nor noise; this per-field band-pass admission is Symbolic-Vector Attention Fusion [11], whose mid-band preference follows the Wundt curve [18]), relevance score si,fs_{i,f}, and emission carrier mjf∈{0,1}m_{j}^{f}\in\{0,1\} indicating whether jj emits field ff. The policy is the pair 𝒜=(α,β)\mathcal{A}=(\alpha,\beta) together with the emission map mm. Everything in the sequel is a property of 𝒜\mathcal{A} and mm.

The carrier mjfm_{j}^{f} is the faithful expression of loss and sovereignty: ii can be influenced by jj on field ff only if jj chose to emit ff. This single term, an emission decision sitting inside the receiver’s update, drives both the convergence and the capability analysis.

Definition 3 (Mesh inference).

Write the local free energy

Li=12​∑j∈Ni∑f∈Fwi​jf​mjf​‖Pf​(oi−oj)‖2+12​μi​‖oi−τi‖2+12​νi​‖oi−𝗆𝖾𝗆i​(q)‖2,L_{i}=\tfrac{1}{2}\sum_{j\in N_{i}}\sum_{f\in F}w_{ij}^{f}\,m_{j}^{f}\,\big\|P_{f}(o_{i}-o_{j})\big\|^{2}+\tfrac{1}{2}\,\mu_{i}\|o_{i}-\tau_{i}\|^{2}+\tfrac{1}{2}\,\nu_{i}\|o_{i}-\mathsf{mem}_{i}(q)\|^{2},

where wi​jf=Ki​j​αi,f​β​(si,f​(oj))≥0w_{ij}^{f}=K_{ij}\,\alpha_{i,f}\,\beta(s_{i,f}(o_{j}))\geq 0 is the per-field admitted weight and mjfm_{j}^{f} the emission carrier, so the coupling term is the gradient of the admission gate AiA_{i}. Here τi\tau_{i} is ii’s private anchor, and 𝗆𝖾𝗆i​(q)\mathsf{mem}_{i}(q) is a question-relevant read-out of ii’s admitted-observation store (the memory term; kept separate from τi\tau_{i} so the private anchor is never conflated with admitted evidence). Each agent descends LiL_{i} through its own emission, treating admitted neighbor observations as fixed data. Mesh inference is the collective relaxation of this coupled free energy: to infer the answer to a question qq, the mesh clamps the question-field coordinates to qq, lets every agent descend its own LiL_{i} in concert, and reads the freed coordinates at the joint equilibrium. We write one such step ask⁡(q)\mathrm{ask}(q), the inference primitive, and the answer is the fixed point the views jointly determine, not a value any member stored.

Because every result below holds for any nonnegative weights, the policy enters the guarantees through its support (which fields each agent admits, wi​jf>0w_{ij}^{f}>0, and emits, mjf=1m_{j}^{f}=1), not through the band-pass magnitudes.

In the linear regime 𝗆𝖾𝗆i​(q)\mathsf{mem}_{i}(q) is a similarity-weighted read-out of the store; replacing this single quadratic term by a log-sum-exp associative energy over the full store is the entire step to the attention-class regime of §12.

4 Property (a): convergence

4.1 Well-posedness of mesh inference

Stack the configuration o=(o1,…,oN)o=(o_{1},\dots,o_{N}). The global Hessian is H=Lw+diag⁡(μi+νi)H=L_{w}+\mathrm{diag}(\mu_{i}+\nu_{i}), where LwL_{w} is the (per-field) admitted-weight graph Laplacian. On a connected graph with some μi>0\mu_{i}>0, H≻0H\succ 0.

Proposition 1 (Every inference has a unique answer).

Partition coordinates into the clamped question set QQ and the free set Q¯\bar{Q}. The restricted problem has Hessian HQ¯​Q¯H_{\bar{Q}\bar{Q}}, a principal submatrix of HH, hence positive definite. So ask⁡(q)\mathrm{ask}(q) has a unique minimizer and terminates, for any νi≥0\nu_{i}\geq 0. Under forwarding the effective operator is the asymmetric M-matrix of Lemma 1 rather than HH; uniqueness persists because that operator is a nonsingular M-matrix on the anchored-reachable component, so the clamped system retains a unique equilibrium.

4.2 The reciprocity spectrum

Whether the relaxation descends a common potential depends on the symmetry of the effective coupling. Three regimes:

  • •

    Symmetric admission (wi​j=wj​iw_{ij}=w_{ji}): the dynamics is exactly the gradient flow of the mesh free energy Φ⁡(o)=12​∑(i,j)∈Ewi​j​‖oi−oj‖2+12​∑iμi​‖oi−τi‖2\Phi(o)=\tfrac{1}{2}\sum_{(i,j)\in E}w_{ij}\|o_{i}-o_{j}\|^{2}+\tfrac{1}{2}\sum_{i}\mu_{i}\|o_{i}-\tau_{i}\|^{2} (a Tikhonov graph-signal denoising energy [16]), which is then a Lyapunov function; on a connected graph Φ\Phi is strongly convex and the unique equilibrium is reached exponentially at rate η​λmin​(H)\eta\,\lambda_{\min}(H).

  • •

    Reversible admission (a positive π\pi exists with πi​wi​j=πj​wj​i\pi_{i}w_{ij}=\pi_{j}w_{ji}): a π\pi-weighted potential survives, extending the guarantee to a strictly larger class.

  • •

    Asymmetric admission: no scalar potential exists, and the quadratic certificate ‖o−o⋆‖2\|o-o^{\star}\|^{2} stops being monotone once the symmetric part of the coupling loses positive definiteness (the anchor diag⁡(μ)\mathrm{diag}(\mu) sets that margin). Convergence itself is not lost. The effective coupling is always a weakly diagonally dominant M-matrix (Lemma 1), so its eigenvalues keep nonnegative real part for any nonnegative weights. Asymmetry costs the common potential and the convergence rate, never stability.

4.3 Convergence under forwarding: a structural argument

Identification (§5) will force agents to re-emit, or forward, admitted directions they did not natively observe, so that information crosses lossy intermediates. Forwarding is an emission-side decision, and in the faithful receiver-autonomous model it is not symmetric: the off-diagonals of the per-field operator are −wi​jf​mjf-w_{ij}^{f}m_{j}^{f} versus −wj​if​mif-w_{ji}^{f}m_{i}^{f}, asymmetric whenever mif≠mjfm_{i}^{f}\neq m_{j}^{f}. The symmetric-potential argument therefore does not apply during propagation; indeed λmin\lambda_{\min} of the operator’s symmetric part goes negative at the propagation frontier. Convergence nonetheless holds, by structure rather than by a common potential.

Lemma 1 (Convergence under non-selective forwarding).

Let agents forward non-selectively: once ii admits a source-novel direction ff it emits ff thereafter, so emission sets grow monotonically E0⊆E1⊆⋯⊆ETE_{0}\subseteq E_{1}\subseteq\cdots\subseteq E_{T}. Then ask⁡(q)\mathrm{ask}(q) converges to the unique anchored equilibrium o⋆o^{\star}, exactly, with finite transient. Anchoring sets the terminal rate through the effective diameter, never the stability.

Proof.

The per-field operator MfM^{f} is a Z-matrix: off-diagonals Mi​jf=−wi​jf​mjf≤0M^{f}_{ij}=-w_{ij}^{f}m_{j}^{f}\leq 0, and row diagonal μi𝟏[obsi=f]+∑jwi​jfmjf\mu_{i}\mathbf{1}[\mathrm{obs}_{i}{=}f]+\sum_{j}w_{ij}^{f}m_{j}^{f} equal to the anchor term plus the row’s off-diagonal magnitude sum. Hence MfM^{f} is weakly diagonally dominant, and on the anchored-reachable component—where an anchored row makes it irreducibly diagonally dominant—a nonsingular M-matrix, so every configuration is itself Hurwitz (Re⁡(λ)>0\mathrm{Re}(\lambda)>0). Two structural facts give convergence with no numerical bound. (i) Finite monotone switching: each carrier mifm_{i}^{f} flips 0→10\to 1 exactly once, at the instant ii first admits a source-novel copy of ff, so the configuration is constant after a finite time TT (≤diam+1\leq\mathrm{diam}+1 distinct configurations along the propagation path), terminating in ETE_{T}, where every carrier-connected pair mutually emits ff and the terminal operator is symmetric positive definite, hence Hurwitz. (ii) Finite-time segments: each of the ≤diam+1\leq\mathrm{diam}+1 configurations is active for a finite time, and a linear ODE with bounded operator carries a finite state to a finite state over a finite interval. The trajectory on [0,T][0,T] is therefore a finite concatenation of finite-time linear-ODE segments, so the state at TT is finite—and this finiteness holds for any switching schedule, since the number of segments is bounded by diam+1\mathrm{diam}+1 regardless of when the switches occur. Within a segment a non-normal MfM^{f} can amplify transiently (supt‖e−Mf​t‖>1\sup_{t}\|e^{-M^{f}t}\|>1, e.g. ≈4.2\approx 4.2 at gain 44), so the transient is finite per instance, not uniformly bounded; its magnitude may grow with diameter, its finiteness does not. From TT onward the terminal symmetric positive-definite operator is Hurwitz and drives exponential convergence to o⋆o^{\star}. ∎

Remark 1.

The M-matrix form is cleaner than a dwell-time argument: with finitely many finite-time segments there is no escape to rule out, so the finiteness of the transient is schedule-independent (its magnitude, set by operator non-normality, may grow with diameter). Selective forwarding (mif≠mjfm_{i}^{f}\neq m_{j}^{f}, including adversarial over-emission) drives the coupling’s symmetric part indefinite past the anchor margin, so the quadratic Lyapunov certificate and the common potential are lost. But the operator remains an M-matrix with eigenvalues in the right half-plane, so it still converges. Selective over-emission slows convergence, since it shrinks the spectral gap, and is lineage-detectable (§7), but it does not destabilize. The one failure that is sharp rather than gradual is loss of carrier connectivity (§5).

4.4 Retrieval rate

Corollary 1 (Latency).

The slowest mode of ask\mathrm{ask} is λmin\lambda_{\min} of the anchored terminal operator. For an anchored path it is the Dirichlet–Laplacian ground mode, λmin≈(π2/4)/N2\lambda_{\min}\approx(\pi^{2}/4)/N^{2} (empirically N2​λmin→2.4N^{2}\lambda_{\min}\to 2.4, matching the path constant π2/4≈2.47\pi^{2}/4\approx 2.47), independent of the anchor strength μ\mu once μ\mu clears the vanishing threshold ∼π2/4​N2\sim\pi^{2}/4N^{2} that separates the weak- from the strong-anchor regime. Hence retrieval latency is O⁡(diam2)O(\mathrm{diam}^{2}), the rate of graph heat-diffusion, set by geometry rather than anchor magnitude. The effective diameter is the distance to the nearest anchor, so denser anchoring shortens it to O⁡(r2)O(r^{2}) in inter-anchor distance rr. Validation therefore buys latency the same way it buys capability: by adding validated anchors that shrink rr, not by raising μ\mu, which above threshold does nothing.

4.5 Asynchronous realization

The relaxation analyzed above is continuous-time. A deployed engine runs asynchronous, discrete message passing, with no global clock and with delayed or dropped messages and node churn. Convergence carries over, by the same M-matrix structure.

Lemma 2 (Asynchronous convergence).

Run the discrete iteration that updates each coordinate by the Jacobi/Gauss–Seidel map of MM, with each node activating at arbitrary times and reading possibly-stale neighbour values. Because M=Lw+diag⁡(μ)M=L_{w}+\operatorname{diag}(\mu) is an irreducibly diagonally-dominant M-matrix, the Jacobi matrix B=I−D−1​MB=I-D^{-1}M (D=diag⁡MD=\operatorname{diag}M) has spectral radius ρ⁡(B)<1\rho(B)<1, so the iteration converges to the continuous fixed point o⋆=M−1​go^{\star}=M^{-1}g for any bounded-delay schedule. If every node is anchored (μi>0\mu_{i}>0), BB is a strict max-norm contraction (‖B‖∞<1\|B\|_{\infty}<1) and convergence is robust to total asynchronism (arbitrary delays [19]): no global clock or reliable delivery is required.

Proof.

MM is a weakly diagonally-dominant Z-matrix (§4), strictly dominant on anchored rows; on a connected graph with an anchor it is irreducibly diagonally dominant, so ρ⁡(B)<1\rho(B)<1 and both the synchronous and bounded-delay asynchronous iterations converge to o⋆o^{\star}. Full anchoring makes every row strictly dominant, so ‖B‖∞=max⁡∑j≠ii⁡|Mi​j|/Mi​i<1\|B\|_{\infty}=\max_{i}\sum_{j\neq i}|M_{ij}|/M_{ii}<1, a max-norm contraction, to which the asynchronous-convergence theorem applies under arbitrary delays. ∎

Remark 2 (Churn is transient disconnection).

A node leaving and rejoining is transient carrier disconnection, a live instance of property (b). While a node is absent its coordinate cannot track, leaving a residual that scales with churn rate and shrinks with anchor density; forwarding re-establishes the carrier when it returns. Anchor density is therefore the single dial for both retrieval latency (Corollary 1) and asynchronous and churn robustness, and anchors are validated observations (§5), so validation buys both. We verify this in simulation. The iteration reaches machine precision under 60%60\% message loss without churn (loss is modeled as staleness until resend, hence bounded delay, which is benign), and the churn residual falls with anchor count, vanishing once the mesh is strictly contractive.

5 Property (b): identification-completeness

We now ask when mesh inference realizes the answer a sovereign population determines collectively: one that exists in the union of views but in no single agent, and which the centralized optimum names. Let each agent hold a lossy view yi=Ci​s⋆y_{i}=C_{i}s^{\star} of a shared latent s⋆s^{\star}. The latent is collectively identifiable when ⋃irow⁡(Ci)\bigcup_{i}\mathrm{row}(C_{i}) is full rank, though each CiC_{i} alone is rank-deficient. This is distributed estimation over a network [15]. The contribution here is not the estimator but the characterization of which admission/emission policies let purely local, sovereign agents realize it—specifically the carrier-graph connectivity criterion (Thm 1), source-novel forwarding, and content-addressed lineage as the sole global side-channel, none of which appear in classical distributed estimation, together with the observation-only dual (§6).

Definition 4 (The mesh’s collective inference).

Let agent ii’s view be its constraint Vi:yi=Ci​s⋆V_{i}\!:\ y_{i}=C_{i}s^{\star} (knowledge of the projection Ci​s⋆C_{i}s^{\star}), and let ⟨⋅⟩\langle\cdot\rangle be the determination operator: ⟨V⟩\langle V\rangle is the set of queries whose answer is fixed by VV, here the row span of its constraints. (The inferential reasoning reading, namely pattern completion and generalization, is the general abstraction this realizes non-linearly in the associative regime, §12.) The collective determines ⟨⋃iVi⟩\langle\bigcup_{i}V_{i}\rangle, each member only ⟨Vi⟩\langle V_{i}\rangle. We formalize the mesh’s collective inference as the closure gap

𝒩=⟨⋃iVi⟩∖⋃i⟨Vi⟩,\mathcal{N}\;=\;\big\langle\textstyle\bigcup_{i}V_{i}\big\rangle\;\setminus\;\textstyle\bigcup_{i}\langle V_{i}\rangle,

the answers fixed by the pooled views but by no member’s own, even after it reasons to exhaustion. Here ask⁡(q)\mathrm{ask}(q) returns qq’s answer in ⟨⋃iVi⟩\langle\bigcup_{i}V_{i}\rangle, which is new knowledge precisely when q∈𝒩q\in\mathcal{N}. The gap is genuine. With AA knowing s1+s2s_{1}{+}s_{2} and BB knowing s1−s2s_{1}{-}s_{2}, neither determines s1s_{1}, yet the pair fixes s1=12​((s1+s2)+(s1−s2))s_{1}=\tfrac{1}{2}\big((s_{1}{+}s_{2})+(s_{1}{-}s_{2})\big), a fact no member holds. The boundary is exact: 𝒩⊆⟨⋃iVi⟩\mathcal{N}\subseteq\langle\bigcup_{i}V_{i}\rangle, so this knowledge is newly derivable, not new information. The collective realizes what its views jointly determine and manufactures nothing beyond them. Collective identifiability (⋃irow⁡(Ci)\bigcup_{i}\mathrm{row}(C_{i}) full rank) is exactly the case ⟨⋃iVi⟩=\langle\bigcup_{i}V_{i}\rangle= the whole of s⋆s^{\star}-space.

5.1 Admission is local; identification is global

A receiver scores incoming fields by novelty against its own anchors. But whether a locally redundant view is globally rank-critical, the piece that completes the union, is invisible locally. Two consequences follow, the second sharper than usually noticed.

Admission must preserve sources, not values.

Redundancy in value space (the numbers look alike) is not redundancy in source space (same origin versus independent observation). Independently sourced corroboration is what builds rank, so it must not be gated. Content-addressed lineage distinguishes the two: with δisrc(oj)=𝟏[roots(lineage(oj))⊈Ri]\delta^{\mathrm{src}}_{i}(o_{j})=\mathbf{1}[\mathrm{roots}(\mathrm{lineage}(o_{j}))\not\subseteq R_{i}], the policy must admit if value-novel or source-novel, and gate only if both are redundant.

Emission must carry, not merely admit.

Hidden state never crosses the wire [10, 12], so an intermediate can recover a rank-critical direction in its private state and never transmit it. The value then dies at an agent that knows it: admission kept the edge open, but nothing carried the value onward. The fix is an emission-side primitive, source-novel forwarding: an agent re-emits an admitted source-novel direction it did not natively observe.

5.2 The carrier graph and the theorem

Definition 5 (Carrier graph).

For an identifying subspace UU, the carrier graph GUG_{U} has edge {i,j}\{i,j\} iff U⊆span⁡(emiti∪emitj)U\subseteq\mathrm{span}(\mathrm{emit}_{i}\cup\mathrm{emit}_{j}) (union masking: one emitting endpoint suffices). When emissions are field-typed and UU is a single field ff, GU=GfG_{U}=G_{f}.

Theorem 1 (Identification-completeness).

Under provenance-aware admission and non-selective source-novel forwarding, ask⁡(q)\mathrm{ask}(q) returns the centralized/Bayes-optimal answer—the conditional mean under the Gaussian model whose prior the anchors τi,μ\tau_{i},\mu encode and whose observation precisions the admitted weights wi​jfw_{ij}^{f} carry—on the collectively-identifiable class iff, for every identifying subspace UU, every observer of UU and every dependent receiver lie in a single connected component of the carrier graph GUG_{U}. Forwarding is exactly the operation that extends GUG_{U} until the component connects; in the full-estimate case (every coordinate emitted) forwarding is automatic and the condition holds trivially. Read through Def. 4, this is a collective-intelligence statement: ask\mathrm{ask} realizes the full collective closure ⟨⋃iVi⟩\langle\bigcup_{i}V_{i}\rangle, deriving every fact in 𝒩\mathcal{N}, including those no member can, iff the views each derivation composes are carrier-connected to the receiver that needs the answer. Connectivity is what lets the reasoning route the fragments together; sever it and the fact falls back to the prior.

Proof (field-typed case).

By Lemma 1 the relaxation runs the directed per-receiver carrier dynamics, but it converges to the equilibrium of its terminal configuration, where every carrier-connected pair mutually emits, which is exactly the union-masked Laplacian of the carrier graph GUG_{U}. So ask\mathrm{ask}’s limit is the minimizer analyzed below, and we may reason on GUG_{U} directly. The objective separates per field; each field ff is an anchored graph-Laplacian solve on GfG_{f}, anchored at the observers of ff. The minimizer returns the true value at node ii iff ii is connected in GfG_{f} to an ff-observer, and the prior otherwise. The general subspace case follows by replacing coordinates with the projectors defining UU. Necessity of forwarding is the witness of §5.1: an intermediate that admits but does not emit leaves GUG_{U} disconnected at itself despite an open admission edge. Exactness of the criterion over native observers, single-crediting of each source, and termination of forwarding are supplied by Lemma 3. ∎

Lemma 3 (Root-identity, termination, and exactness of source-novel forwarding).

Assume content-addressed lineage: a CMB’s identity, hence its root set roots⁡(⋅)\mathrm{roots}(\cdot), is determined by its content and lineage. A native observation by agent kk mints a fresh root and emits {ρk}\{\rho_{k}\}; forwarding re-emits admitted content without incorporating new native data; a remix mints exactly one fresh root per new native datum. Let RiR_{i} be the roots agent ii has admitted, row⁡(Cρ)\mathrm{row}(C_{\rho}) the subspace observed at native root ρ\rho, and reach⁡(i)\mathrm{reach}(i) the native roots whose observer shares ii’s carrier-graph component. Recall source-novelty: oo is source-novel to ii iff roots⁡(o)⊈Ri\mathrm{roots}(o)\not\subseteq R_{i}. Under non-selective source-novel forwarding:

  1. (P1)

    Root-invariance: roots⁡(forward⁡(o))=roots⁡(o)\mathrm{roots}(\mathrm{forward}(o))=\mathrm{roots}(o).

  2. (P2)

    Termination / anti-echo: each agent admits each root at most once, so each admission adds at least one new root to a set bounded by |ℛ||\mathcal{R}| and triggers at most one forwarding event; forwarding halts in ≤|V|⋅|ℛ|\leq|V|\cdot|\mathcal{R}| events, and a pure re-statement (no new root) is never admitted or re-forwarded.

  3. (P3)

    Exactness: the admitted-view subspace at ii equals ∑ρ∈reach⁡(i)row⁡(Cρ)\sum_{\rho\in\mathrm{reach}(i)}\mathrm{row}(C_{\rho}), each native source credited once, independent of path multiplicity.

Consequently the criterion of Theorem 1 is an exact “iff” over native observers: ask⁡(q)\mathrm{ask}(q) returns the centralized optimum iff every native root spanning the identifiable subspace lies in ii’s carrier-graph component.

Proof.

(P1) By content-addressing, roots⁡(⋅)\mathrm{roots}(\cdot) is a function of content and lineage. Forwarding re-emits admitted content with its lineage unchanged (no new native datum), so the re-emission shares the content-address and roots⁡(forward⁡(o))=roots⁡(o)\mathrm{roots}(\mathrm{forward}(o))=\mathrm{roots}(o); a remix unions exactly one fresh root. Thus a forwarded direction retains its root identity across arbitrarily many hops. (P2) A message is admitted as source-novel only if it carries a root ∉Ri\notin R_{i}, and admission adds those new roots to RiR_{i}. Since Ri⊆ℛR_{i}\subseteq\mathcal{R} grows monotonically and roots are never removed, agent ii performs at most |ℛ||\mathcal{R}| admissions, each triggering at most one forwarding event; the total is ≤|V|⋅|ℛ|\leq|V|\cdot|\mathcal{R}|, giving termination. A message whose roots all lie in RiR_{i}, a pure re-statement or a re-forwarded copy of an already-held root, fails source-novelty and is neither admitted nor re-forwarded, so bundling old roots with new ones cannot re-trigger the old. (P3) By (P1) every forwarded copy of ρ\rho carries ρ\rho and lies in row⁡(Cρ)\mathrm{row}(C_{\rho}); by (P2) ii credits ρ\rho once. Path multiplicity therefore cannot inflate rank, since a forwarded copy shares its source’s subspace, while distinct native roots contribute additively, yielding the stated subspace. Finally reach⁡(i)\mathrm{reach}(i) is exactly the native roots in ii’s carrier-graph component, since forwarding (root-preserving by (P1)) extends GUG_{U} precisely along carried roots; so the admitted-view rank equals rank​∑ρ∈reach⁡(i)row⁡(Cρ)\mathrm{rank}\sum_{\rho\in\mathrm{reach}(i)}\mathrm{row}(C_{\rho}), which matches the full-view rank iff every spanning native root lies in ii’s component. The anchored min-norm solve then returns the centralized optimum on precisely that subspace. ∎

Remark 3 (The mechanism is content-addressing).

(P1) is not an extra assumption: content-addressed lineage already determines a CMB’s identity from its content and lineage, so re-emitting admitted content yields the same address and the same roots. The provenance the protocol carries for audit is exactly what makes source-novelty well-defined and forwarding terminating, which is lineage doing one more job. We verify this in simulation: on a cyclic mesh, inherited-root forwarding terminates with each node’s admitted roots equal to its component’s native roots, whereas a fresh-root-per-hop rule (violating (P1)) echoes without bound, forwarding events growing geometrically per round (e.g. 2,4,8,16,…2,4,8,16,\dots on a degree-2 ring); and forwarded copies of one source leave subspace rank unchanged while independent sources add rank.

Remark 4 (Per-subspace, not per-field).

Forwarding must carry the identifying direction, not merely fields it touches: forwarding one axis of a two-axis direction fails. Field-typed emissions (CAT7’s orthogonal projectors) give the clean per-field instantiation, but the criterion is subspace coverage of GUG_{U}.

Remark 5 (Reconciliation with the anti-echo rule).

Source-novel forwarding re-emits content for which the forwarder has no new domain data, which the mesh protocol’s anti-echo rule forbids as paraphrase [10]. The resolution is the value/source distinction on the emission side. A forwarded direction carries an inherited lineage root that is new to the receiver, not a freshly minted one (Lemma 3, P1), even with no new value, so it is not paraphrase. Lineage licenses the forwarding the anti-echo rule would otherwise prohibit, and the rule’s guarantee is preserved because pure re-statements (no new root) stay forbidden. The forwarding rule should additionally be non-selective, so that the carrier graph connects (identification, §5) and the convergence rate is preserved (Lemma 1), a constraint the anti-echo rule does not currently express.

6 Property (c): observation-only

Proposition 2 (Non-transmission).

Every term of ask\mathrm{ask}’s update is a function of agent ii’s own emission, its private anchor τi\tau_{i}, its admitted observations, and its sovereign weights. No neighbor’s hidden state, parameters, or gradients appear in any message. Hence ask\mathrm{ask} returns centralized-equivalent retrieval (Theorem 1) while no node ever transmits its weights, gradients, or raw state.

Non-transmission is structural, true by construction of the wire format, but strictly weaker than confidentiality: an adversary need not be sent a private quantity to reconstruct it from what is sent. The honest question is whether the emission record identifies the private state, and the answer is Property (b) read with the opposite sign.

Definition 6 (Probe-span).

Write the influence of ii’s private vector θi∈ℝd\theta_{i}\in\mathbb{R}^{d} (the part of its data and state that drives its emissions) as oi=Ci​θio_{i}=C_{i}\theta_{i}, lossy with rank⁡Ci≤p<d\operatorname{rank}C_{i}\leq p<d. An adversary coalition induces a set QQ of queries and observes the converged answers ask\mathrm{ask} returns: one rank-≤p\leq p image Ci,q​θiC_{i,q}\theta_{i} per query, not the relaxation transient. The stacked record is C𝒜​θiC_{\mathcal{A}}\theta_{i}, C𝒜=[Ci,q]q∈QC_{\mathcal{A}}=[\,C_{i,q}\,]_{q\in Q}, and the adversary’s probe-span is 𝒫𝒜=row⁡(C𝒜)⊆ℝd\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{A}}=\operatorname{row}(C_{\mathcal{A}})\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{d}.

Proposition 3 (Confidentiality is identification with the opposite sign).

Against an adversary that observes the converged answers (Def. 6), the component of θi\theta_{i} in 𝒫𝒜⟂\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{A}}^{\perp} is non-identifiable: any θi′\theta_{i}^{\prime} with θi′−θi∈𝒫𝒜⟂\theta_{i}^{\prime}-\theta_{i}\in\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{A}}^{\perp} yields an identical record on QQ, so no estimator, at any computational budget, separates them. A single query hides a subspace of dimension ≥d−p\geq d-p, and which directions stay hidden is a structural property of the realizable query family. The result is a dichotomy: either the induced probes span ℝd\mathbb{R}^{d}, and θi\theta_{i} is reconstructed exactly by generically |Q|≳d/p|Q|\gtrsim d/p queries (model inversion), or the clamp structure confines them to a proper subspace (probe-rank deficiency), and the complementary directions are confidential at any budget.

Proof.

By Def. 6 the record is exactly C𝒜​θiC_{\mathcal{A}}\theta_{i}, so it depends on θi\theta_{i} only through its image under C𝒜C_{\mathcal{A}}; two private vectors with equal image are observationally identical, and the indistinguishable set is the coset θi+𝒫𝒜⟂\theta_{i}+\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{A}}^{\perp} of dimension d−dim𝒫𝒜d-\dim\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{A}}. The dichotomy reads off rank⁡C𝒜\operatorname{rank}C_{\mathcal{A}}: ≤p\leq p for one query; =d=d once the induced family spans, which generic queries reach at |Q|≈d/p|Q|\approx d/p; and <d<d permanently when the clamp structure leaves a fixed unprobed subspace, whose complement no budget recovers. Additive emission noise leaves 𝒫𝒜\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{A}} intact, since least squares stays consistent on the spanned subspace, so only noise scaled to a query budget (differential privacy) degrades reconstruction there. Scoping the adversary to the converged output is what makes this exact. A warm start oi​(0)=B​θio_{i}(0)=B\theta_{i} watched through the transient would add the mode e−M​t​oi​(0)e^{-Mt}o_{i}(0) and leak up to rank⁡B\operatorname{rank}B beyond C𝒜C_{\mathcal{A}}, but the query API exposes only the settled answer, not the relaxation path, so that channel is closed by construction. ∎

The bound also covers a participating node that watches relaxation traffic, not only an external querent reading answers: under cold start or warm start from a prior equilibrium, oi​(0)o_{i}(0) is either θi\theta_{i}-independent or a previous query’s image already in 𝒫𝒜\mathcal{P}_{\mathcal{A}}, so the transient mode contributes nothing beyond C𝒜C_{\mathcal{A}}. The rank-BB leak needs a θi\theta_{i}-dependent high-rank initialization the construction never uses.

The rank condition mirrors Theorem 1 exactly: identification needs the union of views full-rank, and confidentiality is the same rank condition with the sign flipped, the private subspace lying outside the adversary’s accumulated span. The connectivity half is an analogy rather than an identity, since the adversary’s probe-span is fixed by the realizable query family, not by the carrier graph; carrier disconnection, which defeats identification, only loosely mirrors the probe-rank deficiency that shields private state. The reading is unsparing. “Observation-only” guarantees non-transmission (Prop. 2) and per-query lossiness, not unconditional secrecy. On the spanning branch of Prop. 3 an adaptive querent mounts a model-inversion attack, while state and parameters that never enter any emission image stay hidden unconditionally. The only defences for the queryable part are structural probe-rank deficiency, a private subspace no admissible query can excite, or query-budgeted noise. The compression axis of §10 is precisely this leakage counted in bits.

This is the guarantee a hosted model structurally cannot match: no raw state, gradients, or weights ever leave a node. We state it with its exact limit rather than as an unconditional moat.

7 The unified characterization

All three are governed by one object, the admission/emission policy, and together they make one thing: a sovereign collective that derives what no member holds (Def. 4), reliably, and without exposing any member. Convergence holds for free. The other two form a dual pair. Identification asks when the collective recovers that answer; confidentiality asks when an adversary cannot recover a private one. Both reduce to the same rank condition read with opposite signs (Fig. 1):

  • •

    convergence is unconditional: the coupling is always an M-matrix (Lemma 1), so it holds for any weights. Reciprocity and non-selective forwarding govern only whether a common potential exists and how fast it converges, never whether it does;

  • •

    identification-completeness needs source-preserving admission and source-novel forwarding with carrier-graph connectivity (Theorem 1). This is the collective-intelligence condition: ask\mathrm{ask} realizes the closure gap 𝒩\mathcal{N}, deriving the answer no member holds, exactly where the views that compose it are carrier-connected to the receiver;

  • •

    observation-only is structural as non-transmission (Prop. 2) and, as confidentiality, the dual of identification (Prop. 3). A private subspace stays hidden exactly where the adversary’s probes fail to span it, the same connectivity-and-rank condition turned to the defender’s favour.

The global information that local agents cannot compute, source-independence and reciprocity, is carried by content-addressed lineage. It is load-bearing four times: constitutive for source-preserving admission, constitutive for legitimate (source-novel) forwarding, the detector of selective forwarding that would thin the carrier graph or slow the rate, and the carrier of the audit trail. Lineage is constitutive for capability (admission and forwarding) and diagnostic for the rate and connectivity it cannot itself enforce. These are distinct strengths, stated as such.

The characterization. Provenance-aware, source-preserving admission together with non-selective source-novel forwarding makes ask\mathrm{ask} identification-complete and observation-only on the collectively-identifiable Gaussian class, with convergence holding unconditionally (Lemma 1) and non-selectivity preserving its rate, and with lineage as the single side-channel that lets purely local agents satisfy a set of globally-defined conditions. This is collective inference as a characterized operation. A sovereign population derives what it jointly knows but no member holds, the answer the centralized optimum names, realized reliably and without exposing any member, on the linear–Gaussian class. It is the inference half of a learning loop (§11): one proven turn of a collective that also acts, learns, and feeds back.

8 Experiments

This section is mechanism verification: the does-the-theory-hold checks. The performance evaluation (accuracy, latency, baselines) is §9. All experiments are synthetic and reproducible. The accuracy experiment of §9 is noisy linear–Gaussian (the centralized optimum is its noise floor); the connectivity, forwarding, M-matrix, and latency experiments are exact (noiseless) algebraic solves.

The intermediate that knows but does not say.

On a chain a−b−ca\!-\!b\!-\!c where the rank-critical direction is observed only by aa and needed by cc, with bb not natively observing it: when bb admits the direction (recovering it exactly in its own estimate) but does not re-emit it, cc recovers nothing; when bb forwards it, cc recovers it exactly. The admission edge was open throughout, so the failure is emission, which isolates the forwarding obligation cleanly. Carrier-graph connectivity predicts the linear solver exactly across chains and a 3×33\times 3 grid, and the quantitative sweep over a forwarding probability pp shows recovery exact while the carrier graph is connected, collapsing to the isolated level only as connectivity is lost (Fig. 2).

Forwarding and convergence.

Across 600600 frontier configurations (chains and grids, random partial-emission frontiers), every carrier-masked operator is a diagonally dominant Z-matrix with Re⁡(λ)≥0\mathrm{Re}(\lambda)\geq 0, and the switched propagation converges to machine precision. Transient amplification is finite and configuration-dependent—a gain-4 asymmetric carrier reaches supt‖e−Mf​t‖≈4.2\sup_{t}\|e^{-M^{f}t}\|\approx 4.2—confirming the finite transient of Lemma 1 without entering its proof. Selective over-emission does not break this. It drives the coupling’s symmetric part indefinite past the anchor margin (a two-node imbalance with gain 44 gives λmin​(Msym)=−0.30\lambda_{\min}(M_{\mathrm{sym}})=-0.30), but MM’s own eigenvalues stay in the right half-plane (there, 5.415.41 and 0.0920.092), so the operator remains an M-matrix and converges. Over-emission only shrinks the spectral gap, slowing convergence (verified up to gain 2020, where min⁡Re​λ=+0.023\min\mathrm{Re}\,\lambda=+0.023). Reciprocity-breaking is likewise benign for accuracy: recovery error stays flat across the full asymmetry sweep, never approaching the isolated level. The single mechanism that collapses recovery is carrier disconnection (Fig. 2).

The phase-encoded case.

With phase emissions the relaxation is the Kuramoto model; coherence rr is negligible below the mean-field critical coupling Kc≈1.60K_{c}\approx 1.60 and rises sharply above it, making the coupling gain an explicit design target: set it above the threshold and the mesh phase-locks.

9 Performance: accuracy, latency, and leakage

The framing of ask\mathrm{ask} as equilibrium inference invites the questions an inference engine is actually judged on: how accurate its answers are against a gold standard, how fast it returns them, and, for a sovereign engine, how much they leak. We report all three on the regime we prove. Accuracy and latency are measured against two baselines: the centralized optimum (one solver pooling every view, the standard a sovereign mesh aims to match) and the isolated agent (no sharing, what it must beat). Confidentiality is measured against an adaptive querent (§6).

Accuracy. Under carrier connectivity, ask\mathrm{ask} realizes the collective answer, which the centralized optimum names, with zero error (Theorem 1). Consider a task no single agent can solve: N=20N{=}20 agents observe a shared latent through rank-deficient views (each rank 2≪62\ll 6, the union full rank), sharing only estimates, never views, models, or gradients. The noisy mesh reaches mean error 0.0410.041, matching the centralized 0.0410.041 exactly, 20×20\times below the isolated 0.8050.805 (Fig. 3a). Sovereignty costs nothing in accuracy: the forwarding fixed point is the centralized optimum exactly (Thm. 1); the cost is the O⁡(diam2)O(\mathrm{diam}^{2}) latency of Fig. 3b. It also degrades gracefully: as forwarding drops, accuracy falls to the isolated level exactly as carrier connectivity is lost, with no intermediate cliff (Fig. 2). Disconnection reverts the unreachable coordinates to the prior, so the answer is less complete, not pulled toward a wrong value.

Latency. Latency is the price of removing the center, and we state it rather than hide it. Retrieval is graph heat-diffusion: the slowest mode is the Dirichlet ground mode λmin≈(π2/4)/N2\lambda_{\min}\approx(\pi^{2}/4)/N^{2}, so convergence takes O⁡(N2)O(N^{2}) iterations in mesh diameter (Fig. 3b; measured log-log slope 1.91.9), against a centralized solve’s single round. The rate is set by geometry, not anchor strength; denser validated anchoring shortens it to O⁡(r2)O(r^{2}) in distance-to-nearest-anchor (Corollary 1), so more validated memory trades directly for lower latency. This O⁡(diam2)O(\mathrm{diam}^{2}) is the cost of the diffusion solver (Jacobi relaxation), not a lower bound on the inference: it reduces to O⁡(diam)O(\mathrm{diam}) under a lineage-routed message-passing realization—exact on tree-like carriers, with loopy carriers inheriting the standard Gaussian belief-propagation convergence caveat—whose mechanism, floor, and scope we state in §12.

Leakage. A sovereign engine is also judged on what repeated queries reconstruct. Each ask exposes a rank-≤p\leq p projection of a node’s private store (Prop. 3), and an adaptive querent accumulates them. Simulated against a node (Fig. 3c), reconstruction error falls from the single-query floor, a hidden subspace of dimension ≥d−p\geq d-p, as the querent’s probes accumulate, reaching machine precision once they span the store at K≈d/pK\approx d/p queries (model inversion). A probe-rank-deficient direction, never an answerable coordinate of any admissible query, stays hidden at every budget. Leakage is thus the dual of identification, dialed by the query budget (§10), not the all-or-nothing secrecy a one-line “observation-only” claim would imply.

Scope. This is performance on the proven linear–Gaussian turn. It is not language-model-grade, and we do not present it as such. The non-convex associative regime, where the loop generalizes a learned answer to a similar problem (§11), is where the open problem lives, and we name it there rather than measure it here.

10 The cost of the construction: a compression–identification–rate frontier

The construction has a genuine internal tension, and we state it rather than hide it. Non-selective forwarding (needed for convergence) and source-novel forwarding (needed for identification) both grow the emission dimension: an agent ends up emitting every source-novel direction it has admitted, pushing pp toward dd.

The two halves of Property (c) (§6) land on opposite sides of this frontier, and saying so sharpens it. Non-transmission (Prop. 2) stands off the frontier: its proof never invokes p<dp<d, so it holds for any emission dimension, p=dp=d included, and sovereignty is invariant. Confidentiality (Prop. 3) is the compression/privacy corner: a richer emission (p→dp\to d) widens each per-query image Ci,qC_{i,q}, so the adversary’s probe-span covers more of the private θi\theta_{i} and the confidential subspace shrinks. What p→dp\to d trades is therefore reconstruction-resistance, privacy counted in bits, and bandwidth, not sovereignty. The qualitative guarantee (non-transmission) is invariant while the quantitative one (confidentiality) moves along the frontier. The frontier is thus three-way, with non-transmission standing off it and confidentiality on its privacy corner:

compression/privacy (small pp, low leakage)  vs  identification (needs forwarding for carrier connectivity, grows pp)  vs  convergence rate (non-selective forwarding keeps the terminal coupling symmetric, so a potential exists at the terminus; selective forwarding only slows, never destabilizes).

Anchor budget is the dial that places a deployment on this frontier: denser anchoring shortens retrieval latency (Corollary 1, via a smaller effective radius rr), while the anchor strength μ\mu sets the margin tolerating selectivity (hence smaller pp, less leakage) before the convergence rate degrades (convergence itself always holds, Lemma 1)—both at the cost of more validated observations. The frontier is the honest limit of the construction. It is also where the associative regime (§12) earns its place, on capacity rather than latency: one-step associative retrieval escapes the diffusion latency that compression aggravates only in the centralized setting, while the sovereign center-free reduction pays the same O⁡(diam)O(\mathrm{diam}) floor (§12).

11 The learning loop

Status. The results of this paper (§4–§10) are one characterized turn of the mesh, proven in the linear–Gaussian regime. This section gives the operational model that turn sits inside. Its dynamics are architecture and open analysis, not theorems, and every claim below is marked.

A deployed mesh does not freeze. An agent asks, and the collective returns its current best answer (proven). The agent applies that answer in the world. What the application teaches is new information, earned empirically rather than produced by the mesh. The agent feeds it back as a fresh observation, which admission, source-novel forwarding, and lineage (§5–§6, the plumbing those sections build) carry to the others. The collective closure can only grow, so the next ask, perhaps for a similar problem, draws on at least as much as the last.

The dynamics [framework].

Give each view a time index Vi​(t)V_{i}(t), and write Vi​(t+1)=Vi​(t)∪{Δi​(t)}V_{i}(t{+}1)=V_{i}(t)\cup\{\Delta_{i}(t)\}, where Δi​(t)\Delta_{i}(t) is the constraint agent ii learned by applying its answer, sourced from the world rather than the mesh. Then ⟨⋃iVi​(t)⟩\langle\bigcup_{i}V_{i}(t)\rangle is nondecreasing, and an ask at tt realizes the closure as it stands (Theorem 1, turn by turn). This is the two-phase shape of equilibrium propagation and active inference [21, 4]. The ask is the inference phase, which reports what the collective currently knows; the feedback is the learning phase, which grows what it knows. Because views only grow and the space is finite-dimensional, the closure stabilizes in finitely many steps. The open question is not whether the loop settles but whether what it settles on is correct.

Why the loop is honest, not magical [the boundary].

The turn manufactures no information: 𝒩⊆⟨⋃iVi⟩\mathcal{N}\subseteq\langle\bigcup_{i}V_{i}\rangle, proven (§5). The collective grows only because agents act in the world and feed back what acting taught them. Information enters through Δi​(t)\Delta_{i}(t), never from the mesh. The mesh is an accumulator of applied collective learning, not an oracle. This is a stronger and more defensible claim than “the collective knows more than its parts,” which stays false at every tt.

Generalization is the open frontier [open].

A similar problem is the step the linear turn does not cover. Matching a learned answer to a problem it was not learned on is the non-linear ⟨⋅⟩\langle\cdot\rangle: the modern-Hopfield and attention regime, an associative energy with exponential capacity and one-step retrieval [17, 9]. In our construction it is the single substitution of the memory term 12​νi​‖oi−𝗆𝖾𝗆i​(q)‖2\tfrac{1}{2}\nu_{i}\|o_{i}-\mathsf{mem}_{i}(q)\|^{2} by a log-sum-exp associative energy over the admitted-observation store. There the collective can derive an upgraded answer beyond any linear combination of views, and that answer can be a confident error: a generative closure derives new knowledge that is true or false, and the loop has no guard that says which. Determination stops being automatic, which is the paper’s central open problem (§12).

12 Scope and the open problem

What is proved is the linear–Gaussian turn. Here ask\mathrm{ask} is a convergent conditional-mean engine that realizes the collective closure ⟨⋃iVi⟩\langle\bigcup_{i}V_{i}\rangle, is identification-complete up to collective identifiability, is observation-only, runs at O⁡(diam2)O(\mathrm{diam}^{2}) latency, and makes every derived answer determined, hence equal to the centralized optimum. What is framework is the loop of §11: the views move, the closure grows by applied feedback, and a similar problem invokes the non-linear closure. The line between them is the line between this paper and its program.

The central open problem: generalization correctness.

When the closure is non-linear, the collective can derive an upgraded answer to a problem no member solved, and it can derive a wrong one with the same confidence. The open problem is when asking improves the collective rather than corrupting it: the conditions under which a generalized answer is guaranteed correct. This is the non-linear analog of the carrier connectivity that makes every answer in the linear turn determined. There is a sharper, dynamical facet. Coupled asynchronous inference and feedback could amplify an error: one fed back, re-admitted, forwarded, and compounded. So correctness must hold not just per answer but under the loop’s own circulation.

Feasibility is not the obstacle.

The non-linear regime’s distributed normalization is not an open problem. The softmax is an associative, center-free reduction [39, 40], not our result and not pursued here. What remains is the sovereign price on the two frontiers the proven results already characterize. Emitting the associative regime’s partial statistics is the model-inversion leak of §6 (the secure-aggregation threat [41]), and a center-free reduction pays the O⁡(diam)O(\mathrm{diam}) latency floor. On the linear side, the O⁡(diam2)O(\mathrm{diam}^{2}) diffusion solver already reduces to that floor under a lineage-routed Gaussian message-passing realization, which is convergent under the same M-matrix condition (Lemma 1) and exact on tree-like carriers [36, 38]. These are the quantitative open items. Generalization correctness is the qualitative one, and the one that decides whether the loop is collective intelligence or confident noise.

Integrity under strategic agents.

The proven properties characterize a mesh whose agents execute the admission/emission policy as specified. Convergence survives deviation—selective and over-emitting carriers still settle (Lemma 1)—but capability does not. A self-interested participant can gate selectively to starve a rival’s view, withhold a forward it owes, or emit observations its own private state does not support, skewing or starving the collective answer. The construction blunts the manipulation it can see: selective forwarding is lineage-detectable (§7), over-emission only shrinks the spectral gap without destabilizing (Lemma 1), and the symmetric regime descends a common potential (§4), the structure potential games [5] exploit. But content-addressed lineage authenticates provenance, not veracity, and detection is not deterrence: a common potential is not a proof that honest emission is each agent’s best reply. The open layer is mechanism design—conditions on the policy, or on a lineage-backed penalty, under which truthful admission and non-selective forwarding are incentive-compatible, an equilibrium no rational or adversarial agent profitably leaves. We supply the detector; that detection suffices to keep the mesh honest is unproven.

13 Conclusion

Mesh inference can be made a well-posed operation. The mesh clamps the question, relaxes a local free energy, and reads the answer. What comes back is what the population knows collectively: the answer its members jointly determine but none holds alone, computed with no center and no member exposed. The conditions under which a sovereign collective realizes that answer reduce to a single characterization of the admission/emission policy (§7), with content-addressed lineage as the only side-channel local agents need. The energy-based inference step and the collective-inference principle both predate us; the contribution is their synthesis under sovereignty, named and proved. Within it, identification and confidentiality are one fact read twice. The carrier connectivity and rank coverage that let the collective derive what no member holds are exactly what bound an adversary’s reconstruction of what a member holds privately. So the condition under which the collective realizes its answer is the condition that keeps each member’s state safe.

That is one turn, and this paper proves it: in the linear–Gaussian regime every answer the collective derives is determined, hence equal to the centralized optimum. But a deployed mesh does not freeze. The turn is the inference half of a learning loop (§11): agents apply the collective’s answer, learn from the world, and feed back, so the closure grows and collective intelligence compounds. It compounds honestly, because information enters by acting, never from the mesh. We formalize that loop as architecture and prove only the turn. We state its frontier here rather than defer it: when does asking improve the collective rather than corrupt it, and can a non-linear collective be trusted to derive an upgraded answer to a similar problem rather than a confident error. The proven turn is the foundation that question stands on. A collective that derives what no member holds, correctly and sovereignly, is the thing a learning loop must not corrupt. Making it learn, provably, is the program this paper opens.
